course_name_original: Redes de Sensores: Aplicaciones Médicas e IoT
course_name_en: Sensor Networks: Medical and IoT Applications

learning_outcomes.text: Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Develop, manage, and lead projects that use data science techniques, tools, and methodologies in different application areas.
Identify opportunities for innovative data-oriented applications in constantly evolving technological environments.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Ability to analyze, encode, process, and transmit information and data using signal processing techniques.
Understand the different communication networks and sensor networks (Internet of Things, IoT) for data capture and transport, mainly those oriented to M2M (machine-to-machine communications).
Understand the basic parameters of communication networks: coverage, bandwidth, transmission techniques, application scenarios.
Be able to characterize transmission mechanisms and phenomena affecting transmission (distortion, noise), as well as techniques to minimize them (encodings, MIMO).

Be able to choose the most suitable data acquisition and transport system for a given application, based on parameters such as coverage area, application scenario, amount of data to be captured and transmitted, real-time requirements.
Ability to discuss the advantages and limitations of communication and sensor network technologies.

Understand the different types of sensors and their applications. Emphasis on medical applications (e-Medicine and e-Health), Smart applications (e.g., Smart-cities), and applications for Industry 4.0.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to wireless networks. Wireless transmission mechanisms and phenomena affecting them (noise, multipath). Access schemes, modulation, coding.
Communication networks for data transport. M2M networks in 4G and 5G. Internet of Things (IoT). Specifications (coverage, frequency bands, bandwidth, access and coding techniques), scope and reach.
Types of sensors and information acquisition elements.
Applications of sensor networks and IoT for data capture and transport.
Applications for Industry 4.0, Smart applications (Smart-Cities and Environmental Management, Smart Buildings), logistics and transport, e-medicine and e-health, open information sources.

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (T1) - Description, project requirements and preliminary design
Practical work (T1) - Development of a sensor subsystem
Practical work (T1) - Development of a monitoring subsystem
Practical work (T1) - Integration and verification of the final system
Practical work (T1) - Intermediate presentation and final demo

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the grade is based on practical work (T1) and a final exam. The practical work includes several components, each with a specified point value. The final exam contributes 1.0 points. For the extraordinary call and differentiated evaluation, there are two parts: a theoretical exam covering all theoretical content (maximum 5 points) and an evaluation of practices through a project with an oral defense (maximum 5 points).
